speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many ex-offenders have been assisted under the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) scheme up to the end of the year 2022; (b) what are the top 10 industries that employ ex-offenders under the JGI; and (c) what steps have been taken to promote a higher take-up rate of the JGI amongst ex-offenders before the scheme expires on 31 March 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The implementation of the JGI has been accompanied by an increase in interest among employers to partner with Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) to hire ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To promote the take-up of the JGI amongst employers for hiring ex-offenders, YRSG has been raising awareness of the JGI and other available support amongst employers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And if so, after the expiry of the JGI in March 2023, I wonder whether the Ministry may want to continue provide incentives for ex-offenders to get into such jobs so that not just they benefit, their families benefit, but society-at-large benefits because we will be able to actualise their potential and ensure as far as possible, that they leave their past behind.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, as I have shared earlier on, ex-offenders have been employed in a fairly wide range of sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The implementation of the JGI has been accompanied by increased also in the number of employers registering with YRSG and then hiring them through YRSG.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: YRSG has also been seeking to on board more companies from the growth sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, quite a sizeable number of them continue to remain in employment nine months after they have first been placed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We feel that this provides very positive and very, very promising insights for us to continue to help them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are reviewing future plans to see how we can help, taking into consideration the economic, the labour market situation as well as the outlook.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some of these programmes include skills training for inmates consisting of combination of literacy skills, critical core skills and technical skills.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Placement services, career retention support, as well as career coaches and advisory services to match inmates with suitable employers and to help them remain gainfully employed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: YRSG continues to establish partnerships and they are recruiting more employers to join them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: By recruiting, by increasing the number of partnerships with employers, we then put out Train and Place and Grow initiative.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We helped to set up training academies in prison and provide capability building opportunities to help supervisors better mentor ex-offender employees.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: MOM, alongside MHA, is looking into other ways to encourage more employers to hire ex-offenders.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member's suggestion in terms of our policy review, we certainly would take them on board.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I think it has benefited something like tens of thousands of firms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, if you look at a magnitude of that part of it, I do not think, by virtue of the fact that it has helped so many people and has uplifted so many people, to then come back and say that, "Oh, as a result of that, our YRSG initiatives are insufficient".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think it is an apple-for-apple comparison.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are a lot of all these considerations that we would take on board and I do not want to front run this thing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are working very closely with agencies on the ground, with MHA; and we will take the suggestions as proposed by the hon Member of Parliament Mr Murali on board as well.
